newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to reopen former Collor aide murder probe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to reopen former Collor aide murder probe.

text.p: A probe into the murder of former Brazilian president Fernando Collor's top aide will be reopened after a new forensic report contradicted the official version that it was a crime of passion, newspapers said on Monday.

The fresh report by four respected forensic experts found no evidence to support the official finding that Paulo Cesar Farias was shot dead by his girlfriend Suzana Marcolino, who then committed suicide, papers said.
According to daily Folha de Sao Paulo, the latest report has prompted judge Alberto Jorge Correia de Lima, who has been handling the case, to announce he will conduct a new investigation.
"The new report carries strong indications of a double homicide, leading the investigations into a new direction," Correia de Lima was quoted by the paper as saying.

Farias became a household name five years ago when the press identified him as the mastermind of an influence-peddling ring that exchanged government favours for money. The revelations led to Collor's resignation in 1992.
Farias and the 28-year-old Marcolino were found dead last year of gunshot wounds at Farias' beach house outside the northeastern city of Maceio in Alagoas state.
The Farias family said it would not comment on the new forensic report, according to O Globo newspaper.
The family has backed the version that Marcolino shot Farias after a lover's quarrel and then turned the gun on herself.
Marcolino's mother and four brothers have left Maceio, O Globo said. They sold their furniture, donated Suzana's clothes and asked friends to forget about the family's existance.
